topics.title: The Muslim Envoy in Madinah

paragraphs.text: We have already spoken about six Madinese who embraced Islam in the pilgrimage season in the eleventh year of Prophethood. They promised to communicate the Message of Islam to their townsfolk. The following year, on the occasion of the pilgrimage, there came a group of twelve disciples ready to acknowledge Muhammad (Peace be upon him) as their Prophet. The group comprised five of the six who had met the Prophet (Peace be upon him) the year before — the sixth who stayed away was Jabir bin 'Abdullah bin Reyab — and the other seven were: Mu'adh bin Al-Harith (Ibn 'Afra), Dhakwan bin 'Abd Al-Qais, 'Ubadah bin As-Samit, Yazeed bin Tha'labah and Al-'Abbas bin 'Ubadah bin Nadalah (all from Khazraj), and Abul Haitham bin At-Taihan and 'Uwaim bin Sa'idah (from Aws).

They avowed their faith in Muhammad (Peace be upon him) as a Prophet and swore: "We will not worship anyone but one Allah; we will not steal; neither will we commit adultery, nor kill our children; we will not utter slander, intentionally forging falsehood; and we will not disobey you in any just matter." When they had taken the pledge, Muhammad (Peace be upon him) said: "He who carries it out, Allah will reward him; and who neglects anything and is afflicted in this world, it may prove redemption for him in the Hereafter; and if the sin remains hidden from the eyes of men and no grief comes to him, then his affair is with Allah. He may forgive him or He may not."

After the Pledge had been taken, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) sent to Yathrib (Madinah) Mus'ab bin 'Umair Al-'Abdari (May Allah be pleased with him), the first Muslim 'ambassador', to teach the people the doctrines of Islam, give them practical guidance, and propagate Islam among those who still professed polytheism. As'ad bin Zurarah hosted him in Madinah. So prepared was the ground, and so zealous the propagation, that Islam spread rapidly from house to house and from tribe to tribe.

One day Mus'ab and As'ad were near a well in the premises of Bani 'Abd Al-Ashhal and Bani Zafar, conversing with some new converts. Sa'd bin Mu'adh and Usaid bin Hudair, chiefs of the two clans, heard of this. Usaid approached the Muslims armed with his lance, cursing, and accused the two men of befooling the weak-hearted. Mus'ab calmly invited him to sit and listen: "If you are pleased with our talk, you can accept it; should you hold it in abhorrence, you could freely immunize yourself against what you hate." "That's fair," said Usaid, pierced his lance in the sand and listened to some verses of the Noble Qur'ân. His face bespoke satisfaction, and he asked how to embrace Islam. They asked him to wash, purify his garment, bear witness to the Truth and perform two Rak'a; he did so, then said there was a man — Sa'd bin Mu'adh — whose people would never hang back if he followed Islam.

Usaid went to Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who could see he had changed, and arranged for the two men to talk with Sa'd privately. The previous scene recurred and Sa'd embraced Islam, then turned to his people swearing he would never talk with them until they believed in Allah and His Messenger. By that evening, all the men and women of that sept had embraced Islam, with the exception of one, Al-Usairim, who hung back until the Day of Uhud — on which he embraced Islam and fought the polytheists, but was killed before observing any prostration in prayer. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) commented: "He has done a little but his reward is great."

Mus'ab stayed in Madinah carrying out his mission diligently and successfully until all the houses of Al-Ansar (the future Helpers) had Muslim members, men and women. One family only stood obdurate to the Islamic Da'wah; they were under the influence of the poet Qais bin Al-Aslat, who screened the Call from their ears until the year 5 A.H. Shortly before the following pilgrimage season — the thirteenth year of Prophethood — Mus'ab bin 'Umair returned to Makkah carrying to the Prophet (Peace be upon him) glad tidings about the new fertile soil of Islam in Madinah and the power and immunity that city was bound to provide to the cause of Islam.

topics.topicSummary: A year after the first six Madinese converted, twelve men came to pledge faith at the First 'Aqabah Pledge, vowing to worship Allah alone and shun major sins. The Prophet ﷺ then sent Mus'ab bin 'Umair as the first Muslim envoy to Madinah, hosted by As'ad bin Zurarah. Through Mus'ab's wisdom, the chiefs Usaid bin Hudair and Sa'd bin Mu'adh embraced Islam — bringing whole clans with them — until scarcely an Ansar household lacked Muslims. Mus'ab returned with glad tidings of Madinah's readiness.

They vowed to worship Allah alone and not steal, commit adultery, kill children, slander, or disobey in just matters
Mus'ab bin 'Umair was sent as the first Muslim envoy ('ambassador') to Madinah, hosted by As'ad bin Zurarah

quiz.question: How many men gave the First 'Aqabah Pledge?
Whom did the Prophet ﷺ send as the first Muslim envoy to Madinah?
Which two Madinese chiefs embraced Islam through Mus'ab, bringing their clans with them?
options: Usaid bin Hudair and Sa'd bin Mu'adh
'Abdullah bin Ubai and Qais bin Al-Aslat
Jabir bin 'Abdullah and Al-Bara' bin Ma'rur
quiz.answer: Usaid bin Hudair and Sa'd bin Mu'adh
